html:
In December 1778 a British force took St Lucia from France and beat off a much larger French fleet and army sent to retake it. The battle was part of the American War of Independence.

St Lucia passed between France and Britain about fourteen times, and was called the Helen of the West Indies. Its harbours, especially Gros Islet Bay below Pigeon Island, were prized for watching the French base on Martinique.

From there Admiral Rodney sailed in 1782 to win the Battle of the Saintes. Britain finally kept the island in 1814. Its French past lives on in the Kweyol language and the Catholic church, as the poems of Derek Walcott often show.
